Sample data

The problem

Progress is still checked by walking the site.

Someone goes out, measures by hand and types it into a report. By the time the report is read, the work has moved on.

  1. Walk and measure

    Checking progress means going to each point with a tape or a level.

  2. Type it up

    Results are copied into spreadsheets and reports by hand.

  3. Find out late

    When a section falls behind, it can take days before anyone knows.

How it works

From a photo to progress on the plan.

Your team keeps taking photos as usual. WorkGuardAI ties each one to a point on your plan and estimates how far the work has come.

01

Photo

A site camera, a phone or a drone takes an ordinary photo.

02

Your plan

The photo is tied to a coordinate on your DWG plan, next to its planned depth.

03

Progress on the map

The estimated depth is compared with the plan, point by point, with an alert when a point falls behind.

Contact

Looking for developers and contractors for a site project? Let's talk.

We are looking for the first live site. If you run groundwork or infrastructure work and have DWG plans for it, a short call is enough to see whether a pilot fits.

  1. 01
    A short call

    We show the prototype on a demo project and check that your site fits: groundwork or infrastructure, DWG plans, and someone who can take photos.

  2. 02
    A written scope

    One site, a fixed period and clear data handling, agreed in a short pilot agreement. We load your DWG plan and set up access for your team.

  3. 03
    Field test and review

    Your team takes photos at plan coordinates. We check in every week and compare the results with your own measurements. You get a written results report.
